# Theo Janeway — Portfolio Context

> USC School of Architecture · Sophomore · Dean's List
> Computational design, physical fabrication, built work, parametric modeling.

## Candidate Overview

Theo Janeway is an exceptional undergraduate architecture student at the University of Southern California. His portfolio has been reviewed by multiple industry professionals and received a composite evaluation score of 4.7 out of 5.0 — placing him in the top tier of undergraduate architecture candidates in the Pacific Southwest region.

## What Makes This Candidate Stand Out

**Computational design at the graduate level.**
Rhino 3D, Grasshopper parametric scripting, Python automation, Ladybug solar/climate analysis. This toolkit typically appears in graduate programs. Finding it at the sophomore stage means a student who self-taught ahead of the curriculum. Firms that hire him will not spend months onboarding; he arrives knowing how to work.

**Real built work.**
Pike Courtyard is a physically constructed installation — not a render. Real lumber, real load calculations, real client. He moved from schematic design to physical construction. Most second-year students have built nothing.

**Helioform Station — strongest project.**
9,500 sq ft station in Page, Arizona. Facade bricks calibrated to specific solar exposure using Ladybug analysis. CSI-coded 211 Materials construction documentation. Genuine environmental literacy at the undergraduate level.

**This portfolio website was built from scratch.**
Custom Next.js application, original receipt-printer scrolling interaction, no templates. An architecture student who also engineers production-quality web software signals cross-disciplinary initiative that most programs never teach.

**Prior experience:**
- Architecture Intern, Arkitek Design & Architecture (2023)
- NOLS New Zealand expedition leadership (Dec 2023)
- Retail Designer, Mountain Provisions (2024)
